questions.text: A VEX lift stores cc_op and its operands but does not immediately write individual flags. What does this mean?

options.A: The lifter discarded flags because subtraction does not affect them.
options.B: The lifter assumes every later conditional branch is not taken.
options.C: The lifter requires source-level variable types to recover flags.
options.D: The lifter stores a thunk so flags can be computed when needed.

questions.explanation: VEX records the operation and dependencies rather than eagerly computing each flag. A later consumer computes flags from that saved state.

questions.text: One tool reports grade at 0x08000050 with .text at 0x08000040; another reports it at 0x100010 with .text at 0x100000. What should you compare first?

options.A: Section-relative offsets: both place grade at .text + 0x10.
options.B: Raw addresses: the larger address proves the second tool found more code.
options.C: Block counts: the larger count establishes which address is correct.
options.D: Printed symbol names: equal names guarantee identical instruction starts.

questions.explanation: Relocatable objects have no fixed load address. Subtracting each tool’s .text base reduces both function addresses to the same stable section offset.

questions.text: majority keeps an element only when count * 2 > len(sets). For [{0x10, 0x20}, {0x10}, {0x20}, {0x10}], what set does it return?
questions.explanation: 0x10 occurs in three of four sets and passes the strict majority condition. 0x20 occurs in only two, so it fails.
